objective: Establish how many independent published routes exist to the Martin and Moyce square column collapse data, and re-take the F7a verdict against the best of them, before any further compute is spent refining a mesh against a reference this lab has never read
rationale: The dam break gate is the blocking rung of the whole naval ladder, and it fails by 11.03 percent against a reference whose provenance is weaker than the verdict resting on it. The eight comparison points were digitised, twice and carefully, from a figure in a secondary source; the primary paper is recorded in our own specification as not open access and never read by this lab. The dam break literature places this configuration's data in the primary paper's own tables rather than in a figure, which if true means the current reference is a digitisation of a rendering of a table that exists. Two further facts point the same way. First, the comparator's own published simulation, given our solver the comparator's physics on the comparator's mesh in the comparator's domain, sits 23.3 percent away from us, an offset more than twice the residual the campaign has been chasing. Second, the re-gate already recommended against buying a 760 to 1,520 core minute refinement rung on exactly the grounds that it explores a direction shown to be small. What has never been done is the cheap thing: ask whether the reference itself is where the disagreement lives. If it is, the naval ladder unblocks at zero compute and three filed naval proposals stop being blocked behind a rung that was failing against the wrong numbers. If it is not, the failure is physics, the verdict hardens, and the direction dies for the cost of a literature pass
gate: Zero-compute, and the deliverable is a provenance table before it is a verdict. Stage 1: enumerate every published route to the Martin and Moyce (1952) square-column data for the 2a-high by 1a-wide column, and CLASS EACH BY ITS ROUTE -- primary tables read directly, a re-tabulation by a later author who read the tables, or a digitisation of a figure. Two sources that both digitised the same figure are ONE route, not two, and the table must say so. Stage 2: PASS (reference exonerated, direction dies) if at least two independent routes agree with the frozen eight-point table within the digitisation tolerance already recorded for it, 0.01 in dimensionless time and 0.005 in dimensionless height. In that case the +11.03% FAIL is physics and this item closes having removed a doubt. FAIL (reference disputed) if two independent routes disagree with the frozen table, or with each other, by more than 5% at any graded station -- 5% being the gate's own tolerance, so a reference spread that wide means the gate is not decidable against this benchmark at all, and rung S0 must move to a different case rather than be refined toward. NO VERDICT if no second independent route exists in the open literature: the benchmark is then single-sourced for us, which is itself the finding and is reported as one rather than resolved by picking a favourite. Stage 3, only if Stage 2 returns FAIL: re-take the F7a verdict against the corrected table using the tracked field data, changing nothing else, exactly as the re-gate took its verdict at zero compute. IDENTITY TEST, per Verification Charter 2a. Q1, what makes this FAIL: independent sources agreeing with the frozen table. Q2, could a wrong treatment still pass? Yes, by one specific route -- counting two sources as independent when both digitised the same figure, which would manufacture agreement out of a single origin. That is why route classification is gated and mere source-counting is not. EXTERNAL REFERENT, per Verification Charter 6a: the entire item IS an external referent audit; the referent is Martin and Moyce (1952), Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A, volume 244, pages 312 to 324, and the honest disclosure is that access to it is UNVERIFIED and may fail, in which case the item reports what it could and could not obtain.
cost_basis: Zero solver compute, and the basis is that the machinery to spend it has already been proven unnecessary here: the re-gate produced its verdict at zero core minutes from field data already tracked in the repository, so re-grading against a corrected reference table is arithmetic over data on disk and not a solve. The cost is agent time on a bounded literature pass plus that arithmetic. Stated against the alternative it displaces: the refinement rung this replaces was priced at 760 to 1,520 core minutes, two to four times the entire campaign that preceded it, and was recommended against on measured grounds
expected_knowledge_gain: The single blocking rung of the naval ladder either unblocks or hardens, and either outcome is bought at no compute. Three filed naval proposals, together carrying several thousand core minutes, sit behind this rung under the ladder rule; knowing whether it fails for a real reason is worth more than any of them individually. There is a second gain that outlasts the case: this lab currently grades a naval verdict against points digitised twice from a secondary source's figure, and carries that limitation honestly on the verdict's face. Turning an honest caveat into a measured provenance table is the concrete form of the referent-travels-with-the-verdict clause adopted today, applied to the one gate where it decides whether money gets spent
hard_criterion_note: Starts no flow case. Stage 3 re-grades existing tracked field data if and only if stage 2 disputes the reference, which is arithmetic over a completed run rather than a new one

launch_prompt: F7a reference triangulation. ZERO COMPUTE unless stage 2 returns FAIL, and even then no solver runs -- stage 3 is arithmetic over tracked fields. Step 1: read demo-output/website/campaign/F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md in full, especially the comparison-basis section, and copy out the frozen eight-point table and the two-digitisation tolerance. Step 2: literature pass. Try to obtain Martin & Moyce (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. A 244:312-324 itself; log every access route attempted and its outcome, in the manner the Dow access list already establishes. Then find every OTHER published rendering of the 2a-by-1a square-column data. For each, record the route: did that author read the tables, re-tabulate from someone who did, or digitise a figure? Step 3: build the provenance table and apply the three-valued verdict. Two sources that digitised the same figure are ONE route. Step 4, only on FAIL: re-take the verdict against the corrected table using the tracked fields under demo-output/website/campaign/F7_runs/, changing NOTHING else in the spec -- the spec is a frozen pre-registration and you may not adjust a threshold, a station set or an axis to fit a new reference. If the corrected reference would require a spec change, say so and STOP; that is Katie's call. FILE NOTHING EXTERNALLY, register nothing, email nobody. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, docket update, and if the reference is exonerated say so plainly and close the item.
